newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's rebel leader arrives in mining capital.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's rebel leader arrives in mining capital.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila arrived in Lubumbashi on Monday for what was expected to be a tumultuous welcome from the people of the country's second city taken over by his forces last week.

The capital of mineral rich Shaba province, a city of over one million, is Kabila's biggest prize to date but perhaps his trickiest political challenge. Some factions on Monday accused him of trampling on their political rights by appointing an interim governor in the province instead of holding immediate elections.

Heavily armed troops of the rebel army were posted in the tall grass on both sides of the road leading from the airport into the city to provide security for Kabila. Church bells were rung and hundreds of curious onlookers cheered as a convoy of cars carrying Kabila swept by.

The rebel leader was expected to hold a victory rally in Lubumbashi, formerly the Belgian-Congo town of Elisabethville. He effectively controls over half of Zaire, a country the size of Western Europe.

On Sunday, ministers of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) flew into Lubumbashi and announced over local television that Gaetan Kakudji would act as interim governor.

An AFDL spokesman, who declined to elaborate on the appointment, said "confusion" among the people precluded an instant election of local administrators such as the alliance had carried out in regions taken earlier in the six-month-old revolt to topple the regime of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
